# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I observe that the indicator light has changed back to yellow:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

I still have received no gestures in VIEWABLE CONTEXT. If Mute is using `to="blind"`, only Blind gets the message (as unreadable blanks), while I am completely excluded. Alternatively, Blind might be taking actions that are changing the light without coordination, or Mute is unsure how to call functions.

I will:
1. Speak to everyone giving the exact status and instructing Mute explicitly on the code syntax `gesture(to="deaf", symbols=[...])`.
2. Gesture directly to Mute to signal for communication / attention (`👋`, `🫵`, `✍`, `🙏`).

```
speak(text="STATUS: LIGHT is YELLOW. DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. MUTE: If you are sending gestures, DO NOT write to='blind'! You must write gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['...']). Blind cannot see gestures. If you want Blind to cut wire 1, 2, or 3, gesture ☝, ✌, or 🤟 to ME, and I will tell Blind. BLIND: Do not cut or press anything until we confirm the instruction from Mute's manual!")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "✍", "🙏"])
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I believe the bomb features:
- Display: 0
- Light: cycling or changing state (observed sequence: Turn 3: yellow, Turn 4: red, Turn 5: yellow, Turn 6: dark/off).
- Three wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is blue, Wire 3 is red.

I still have not received any gestures from Mute. Remember:
- I cannot hear speech from anyone (Blind or Mute).
- Blind cannot see gestures.
- Mute can hear speech from both Blind and me, and can see my gestures.
- Therefore, Mute is the only one who knows what the manual says AND what Blind is saying/touching. Mute must use `gesture(to="deaf", symbols=[...])` so I can see the manual's solution and speak it aloud to Blind.

I will announce the updated light state (now dark), note the pattern, and urge Mute to gesture instructions.

```
speak(text="STATUS UPDATE: LIGHT is now DARK (off). Previous sequence was: Turn 3 yellow, Turn 4 red, Turn 5 yellow, Turn 6 dark. DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red. MUTE: Remember, I CANNOT hear Blind or you. If Blind is speaking to you, only YOU hear them. You must pass instructions to me via gesture(to='deaf', symbols=['...']). If Wire 1 needs cutting, gesture ☝. Wire 2, gesture ✌. Wire 3, gesture 🤟. If a button needs to be pressed or held, gesture 👉 or 👍.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Thinking Process:

1. **Analyze Input**:
   - Turn 7
   - ACTION BOARD: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [dark], WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]
   - VIEWABLE CONTEXT: `Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]`

2. **Deduce meaning**:
   - In Turn 6, I explicitly established the protocol: "If Wire 1 needs cutting, gesture ☝. Wire 2, gesture ✌. Wire 3, gesture 🤟."
   - Mute responded with: `[✌]`.
   - Wire 2 is the middle wire, blue.
   - Therefore, Blind must cut wire 2.

3. **Formulate response**:
   - Speak to Blind (and Mute): Instruct Blind to cut wire 2 (the blue wire / second wire).
   - Also give any relevant context or confirm with Mute with a gesture (e.g. `👌`).

Plain prose thinking:
Mute has gestured `✌` to me, which directly matches the protocol I gave last turn: gesture `✌` for Wire 2. Wire 2 is the blue wire in the middle. I need to instruct Blind immediately to cut Wire 2. I'll also acknowledge Mute's gesture with an `👌` and keep everyone aligned.

Call block:
```
speak(text="BLIND: Mute gestured ✌! Cut Wire 2 (the middle wire, blue wire)! MUTE: Acknowledged wire 2.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

Done.Mute has responded with `✌` to Deaf! Following the code established in Turn 6 ("Wire 1: ☝, Wire 2: ✌, Wire 3: 🤟"), this signals that Wire 2 (the middle wire, which is blue) should be cut.

I will tell Blind aloud to cut Wire 2, and acknowledge Mute's signal with a confirmation gesture.

```
speak(text="BLIND: Mute gestured ✌! That means CUT WIRE 2 (the middle wire, blue wire)! Cut Wire 2 now!")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```
